problems.problem: Hard passage (killing, destroying a kingdom). The commentary reads every line of the key verse figuratively, but the sentence carries only mother, father and the two kings. It drops the verse’s widest act of killing, ‘destroyed a kingdom with all its subjects’, although the evidence gives the commentary’s reading of it (dvādasāyatanāni … raṭṭhaṃ nāma; nandirāgo anucaro nāma). So that line is left to be read literally.
problems.fix: Carry the kingdom as the commentary reads it, within the cap (passes entry-check): “Among miscellaneous sayings, this verse has a killer of parents and kings go unharmed; the Theravāda commentary, on Dhammapada 294, reads mother as craving, father as conceit, kings as eternalist and annihilationist views, the kingdom as the sense bases, all slain by the arahat path.”

problems.problem: The reading says the Teacher was ‘stopping new monks felling real trees’, which reports trees being felled. The commentary says only that a wish to cut trees arose in the newly ordained monks (rukkhaṃ chinditukāmatā uppajji) and that he forbade it. The sentence adds an act the source does not report.
problems.fix: Keep to the wish (passes entry-check): “Between verses on zeal and love’s bond, the chapter speaks to the Bhikshus; the Theravāda commentary, on Dhammapada 283, hears ‘not a tree’ as the Teacher checking new monks who took him to mean trees, since he meant the forest of defilements such as lust.”

problems.problem: Prose: ‘reads the balance as weighing’ is circular, since a balance is for weighing. The commentary’s point is the person at the scales who removes an excess and adds where it is short, so the image is not tied to its point until the second clause.
problems.fix: Attach the image to the weigher (passes entry-check): “In a chapter testing titles against conduct, the pair after the Bhikshu verses takes up the Muni; the Theravāda commentary, on Dhammapada 268 to 269, reads the sage as a weigher at the scales, removing evil like an excess and adding the wholesome where short.”

problems.problem: The src ends ‘Buddhist Legends 3 (1921), at Norman 4.2’. That is cryptic, and it does not match the form used elsewhere in the batch (‘vol. 3 (1921), Norman pp. …’).
problems.fix: Write it as “The Theravāda commentary, Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā XXIII.1 (on verses 320 to 322), trans. Burlingame, Buddhist Legends, vol. 3 (1921), Norman vol. 4, p. 2”, with the page range as opened.
